sets.title: Failure-safe module initialization

objective_text.T57.01.a: Derive and defend: Show each owned bit has exactly one release and no release precedes its dependents. Relate O(3) model work to the number of real acquisitions, including a failure before endpoint publication.
objective_text.T57.01.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_unwind for an ownership mask whose bits0,1,2 mean buffer, workqueue and registered endpoint. Return the decimal release trace with resource numbers3,2,1 in reverse order; unknown bits return0. Derive the acquire/fail matrix, then apply it to the supplied teaching module init labels.

Then Replace one acquisition by a managed device allocation and demonstrate which cleanup obligations migrate to the device lifecycle, including failure after publication.

sets.title: User-copy progress and ABI admission

objective_text.T57.02.a: Derive and defend: State ownership of unread input, modified prefix and untouched suffix. Explain why a partial-copy return cannot be reused as a negative errno and why cap admission precedes copying.
objective_text.T57.02.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_copy into a live disjoint destination with capacity cap. Reject n>cap with -1 before writes; otherwise copy min(n,fault_after) bytes and return the completed count. The model input is ordinary accessible memory; a separate guest adapter must use copy_from_user and preserve its actual return convention.
objective_text.T57.02.c: Falsify and transfer: A faulty wrapper returns the requested count after a partial copy and exposes stale bytes. Demonstrate the stale sentinel in the original local teaching endpoint without touching other processes. Then Change the ABI to all-or-nothing record publication using private staging; inject a fault after a valid header and show no record becomes visible.

sets.title: Reference acquisition before handoff

objective_text.T57.03.a: Derive and defend: Associate every reference with a named owner; count conservation is initial plus successful acquires minus releases. Explain why a nonzero count cannot validate a pointer that may already be freed.
objective_text.T57.03.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_ref with op0 acquire and op1 release for a live KLRef initialized to {1,0}. Reject unknown operations, zero/dead acquisition and UINT_MAX overflow; reject repeated release. Last release sets dead exactly once. Failed transitions preserve the struct. Map each transition to kref_init/get/put and protected lookup in the VM adapter.
objective_text.T57.03.c: Falsify and transfer: Reject resurrection after the terminal release and a get-after-handoff schedule. Delaying free alone masks the race without creating valid ownership. Then Add a lookup table and compare mutex-protected get-unless-zero with RCU-protected storage lifetime; show why refcount and grace period solve different obligations.

sets.title: Context-sensitive locking

objective_text.T57.04.a: Derive and defend: Derive preemption, migration, interrupt and inter-CPU exclusion separately. A lockdep trace is evidence for exercised lock-order paths, not a proof of all schedules.
objective_text.T57.04.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_lock_allowed(context,kind,rt) for conservative teaching policy: context0 task,1 hardirq,2 softirq; kind0 mutex,1 spinlock_t,2 raw_spinlock_t. Mutex is task-only; raw lock is allowed in all three; ordinary spin lock is allowed in all non-RT contexts and only task context in this restricted RT exercise. Reject out-of-range fields. Defend why the policy is deliberately narrower than all Linux APIs.
objective_text.T57.04.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair an RT hardirq path that uses ordinary spinlock_t and a second-core race hidden by local interrupt disabling. The host truth table assesses policy only. Then Move a callback from task context to threaded IRQ and then hardirq; revise allocation and lock choices and retain the failed and corrected guest traces.

sets.title: Work cancellation and terminal ownership

objective_text.T57.05.a: Derive and defend: Prove release implies quiescence and closed admission. Compare cancellation return values with work ownership; do not hold a lock required by the worker while synchronously draining it.
objective_text.T57.05.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_work for serialized state {queued,running,closed,released}. Events0 submit,1 begin,2 complete,3 close,4 release. Admission fails when closed or occupied; begin transfers queued to running; complete requires running; close is idempotent; release succeeds only once when closed and neither queued nor running. Rejected events preserve state.
objective_text.T57.05.c: Falsify and transfer: A faulty release ignores running work after close; the sentinel release flag demonstrates premature destruction. A deadlock also occurs if teardown waits while holding the worker lock. Then Allow a worker to requeue itself; introduce a closure generation and prove no requeue survives the close linearization point.

checklist: Do not free until the final possible callback is quiescent; synchronous cancellation has its own lock constraints.

sets.title: RCU read-side lifetime model

objective_text.T57.06.a: Derive and defend: Show removal prevents new lookup while preexisting readers retain storage lifetime. Identify how refcount acquisition extends ownership beyond a read-side section and why the section alone does not do so.
objective_text.T57.06.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_grace with events0 enter reader bit id0..7,1 leave,2 retire,3 reclaim. Enter rejects duplicate IDs and admission after retirement; leave requires membership. Retirement is idempotent. Reclaim succeeds only after retirement with no readers and clears retired. This fixed-reader model is intentionally stronger than general RCU and must be mapped critically to the real primitive.
objective_text.T57.06.c: Falsify and transfer: Repair immediate reclamation on unlink; delayed arbitrary sleeps are not grace-period proofs. Host bitmask traces cannot validate actual RCU memory ordering. Then Permit readers of a replacement object after retirement; tag reader epochs and show waiting for all new readers can cause unnecessary starvation.

checklist: Wait for the appropriate grace condition, not an assumed duration.

sets.title: Versioned kernel control records

objective_text.T57.07.a: Derive and defend: Demonstrate exact-length admission and byte-order independence; distinguish ABI versioning from ISO C object representation and kernel/user pointer validation.
objective_text.T57.07.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_decode on octets [version=1,length=2,lo,hi]. Require exactly4 bytes, decode little-endian16 into unsigned output, and leave it unchanged on all rejection. Then design a fixed-width ioctl or read/write adapter without embedding host pointers, documenting compatibility behavior.

A correctly decoded version does not authorize an operation. Then Add a version2 optional field while preserving version1 bytes; compare strict rejection, ignorable extensions and per-operation authorization with adversarial tails.

sets.title: Unload defense and integrated lifetime audit

objective_text.T57.08.a: Derive and defend: Construct a global ownership graph and identify the linearization point of shutdown. Give separate evidence for module pinning, object release, callback quiescence and bounded wait policy.
objective_text.T57.08.b: Implement and investigate: Implement kl_can_unload(open_handles,pending_callbacks,closed) returning true only for closed==1 and both counts zero. Reject closed>1. Integrate the previous model with the teaching module: enumerate every close, completion and last-put ordering and provide a guest unload dossier showing why no callback can reach released state or unloaded text.
objective_text.T57.08.c: Falsify and transfer: A module unloads after the last open handle while a callback still retains its function pointer. Demonstrate rejection in the model; any guest fault stays inside the disposable VM. Then Add hot-unplug while two open handles remain: choose revoked operations versus retained detached objects, and justify error propagation and final cleanup under both close orders.
